title: Beyond Data: Imperfect Physics as a Prior for Reinforcement Learning
detail: Reinforcement learning (RL) promises agents that can improve through experience using only the supervision provided by a reward function. In robotics, however, real-world interaction is expensive, dense rewards are difficult to specify, and sparse rewards often lead to sample-inefficient learning. In this talk, I explore whether imperfect physics priors can nevertheless provide useful structure for RL.  Focusing on goal-conditioned RL (GCRL) for robot navigation and manipulation, I show how control-theoretic principles can serve as inductive biases for policy learning. We first connect goal-reaching value functions to time-to-go fields and interpret the Eikonal equation as a simplified surrogate for the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, motivating Eikonal-informed value learning for challenging navigation problems. We then study its interaction with the quasimetric structure typical of GCRL. Their combination reveals the limitations of imposing these priors globally and motivates a hierarchical formulation. This becomes particularly important in contact-rich manipulation, where hybrid dynamics induce state-dependent controllability and motivate applying physics-informed structure only to appropriate state representations.
speaker: Vittorio Giammarino
bio: Vittorio Giammarino is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Industrial and Management Systems Engineering at the University of South Florida, where he leads the Learning-enabled Autonomy (LEA) Lab. His research lies at the intersection of Reinforcement Learning and Control Theory with a focus on developing data-efficient, safe, and physically grounded learning methods for autonomous systems. Before joining USF, he was a Postdoctoral Research Associate at Purdue University. He received his Ph.D. in Systems Engineering from Boston University, his M.Sc. in Systems and Control from TU Delft, and his B.Sc. in Automation Engineering.
